units.source_text: 亲王的宫邸本来宽广华丽。

en.t: The prince's residence had originally been spacious and splendid.

units.source_text: 其中池塘、假山等，面貌犹无异于当年，然而一天比一天荒凉了。

en.t: Its ponds, artificial hills, and other features still looked much as they had in former days, yet the place grew more desolate day by day.

units.source_text: 亲王寂寞无聊之时，只在此中闲眺怅望。

en.t: When the prince felt lonely and weary, he would do nothing but gaze out idly and sadly there.

units.source_text: 家臣中已经没有干练的人，庭院无人打扫整理，杂草青青，异常繁茂。

en.t: There were no longer any capable retainers in his household, and with no one to sweep or tend the garden, the green weeds grew extraordinarily thick.

units.source_text: 屋檐下的羊齿植物得其所哉，欣欣向荣地到处蔓延。

en.t: The ferns beneath the eaves seemed to have found their proper home and spread everywhere in luxuriant growth.

units.source_text: 四时花木，例如春天的樱花、秋天的红叶，往时与同心人共赏其香色，获得安慰甚多。

en.t: The flowers and trees of the four seasons, such as spring cherry blossoms and autumn maples, had once brought him much comfort when he admired their fragrance and colors with one who shared his heart.

units.source_text: 今则孤居寂处，无人相伴，惟有专心于家中佛堂内的装饰，晨夕诵经礼佛。

en.t: Now he lived alone in seclusion with no companion, devoting himself only to adorning the household chapel and reciting sutras and worshipping the Buddha morning and evening.

units.source_text: 他常常想：“我受二女牵累，已是意外的憾事，自知此乃前世注定，不得如意称心。

en.t: He often thought, "It is already an unexpected regret that I am bound by my two daughters, and I know this was destined from a former life, leaving me unable to have things as I wish.

units.source_text: 岂宜效仿世人，更作续弦之想？”

en.t: How could I properly imitate ordinary people and think of taking another wife?"

units.source_text: 年月既久，越发背世离俗，他的心已经变成了一个高僧。

en.t: As the years passed, he withdrew ever further from the world and its ways, until his heart had become that of a lofty monk.

units.source_text: 自从夫人逝世以来，他即使偶尔戏耍，也不发生世俗续弦之念。

en.t: Since his wife's death, even if he occasionally amused himself, no worldly thought of remarriage arose in him.

units.source_text: 别人劝谏他：“何必如此呢？

en.t: Others admonished him, saying, "Why must you go so far?

units.source_text: 死别之初，固然有无穷悲恸，但日月既经，哀思自会消失。

en.t: At first, after a bereavement, grief is naturally boundless, but once months and years have passed, sorrow will fade of itself.

units.source_text: 还不如回心转意，随俗行事。

en.t: It would be better to change your mind and act according to ordinary custom.

units.source_text: 则此荒凉不堪入目之宫邸，自会重新生色。”

en.t: Then this residence, now so desolate that one can hardly bear to look at it, would naturally regain its vitality."

units.source_text: 他们头头是道地说了许多话，屡次前来做媒。

en.t: They spoke at great length and with an air of reason, and came many times to arrange a match for him.
But the prince turned a deaf ear.
